note: 衣類 is somewhat formal; 服 is the common everyday word for clothes or clothing (ent_seq:1500940).
夢想する suggests fantasizing; 願う directly means to hope or wish (ent_seq:1217950).
重さ is the standard Japanese term for weight, including an object's gravitational weight; trọng lượng is the precise Vietnamese scientific term.
捜索 often means an organized search for someone or something missing; 探索 more generally means a search or hunt to find something (ent_seq:1418340).
The Vietnamese has the wrong tone mark: mổi is incorrect here; mỗi ngày is the standard phrase for every day.
作用する means act upon or have an effect; 機能 is function and is used as a suru verb for to function (ent_seq:1221130).
バジェット is uncommon in general Japanese; 予算 is the standard everyday word for a budget (ent_seq:1543000).
校長 and hiệu trưởng are standard equivalents for a headteacher; the English male specification is contextual rather than a separate lexical term here.
拾う and nhặt suggest picking something up from the ground; 持ち上げる means lift (ent_seq:1315610), and nhấc lên is the general Vietnamese lift-up phrase.
私自身 directly means myself (ent_seq:1311200); bản thân tôi makes the first-person self-reference explicit, unlike generic mình.
こと and việc are very general things or matters; 事柄 means an affair or circumstance (ent_seq:1314240), and vấn đề fits a matter of concern or problem.
nhá is informal and less common; nhai is the standard Vietnamese verb for chewing and is attested in vn_freq (rank 3973).
tài xế is a general driver; tài xế riêng expresses the privately employed or dedicated driver specified here.
人形 and búp bê are the standard words for a human-shaped figure used as a toy; the puppet sense is separate.
拡充 implies enrichment or strengthening; 拡大 is the general noun for expansion or extension (ent_seq:1205200).
射す refers to light rays falling on something; 輝く is the general verb to shine or glisten (ent_seq:1224020).
照る is mainly used of the sun or moon; 輝く is the general verb to shine or glisten (ent_seq:1224020).
日陰 means an area out of the sun; 陰 read かげ directly covers shade and shadow (ent_seq:1590150).
鉢 directly means a bowl, pot, or basin, matching the stated general container sense.
反省 often implies self-criticism about past actions; 省察 means reflection or consideration more generally (ent_seq:1351080).
見掛け is a noun for outward appearance, not an adjective; apparent also means obvious or seeming, and no intended sense is specified.
改める is a broad change or alteration; 改訂 is specifically revision of text and is used as a suru verb (ent_seq:1201060).
hay can mean good or nice generally; thú vị specifically means interesting or fascinating and is attested in vn_freq (rank 845).
抱擁する is formal; 抱きしめる is the common verb to hug or embrace someone (ent_seq:1516320).
破片 usually means a physical shard; 断片 also covers an imperfect or abstract fragment (ent_seq:1419790).
症候 is formal or technical; 症状 is the usual everyday word for a symptom or a patient's condition (ent_seq:1351030).
住宅 often means a residential building or housing; 住居 directly means one's dwelling or residence (ent_seq:2841455).
縄 usually means rope and suggests a thicker cord; 紐 directly means string or cord (ent_seq:1487970).
爪 and móng are the standard terms for nails on human fingers and toes; the other animal structures are separate senses.
毛皮 often suggests fur or pelt as material; 体毛 means body hair (ent_seq:1953420), and lông thú specifies animal fur rather than hair generally.
レギュラー is common only in certain product or role contexts; 普通 directly means normal, ordinary, regular, or usual (ent_seq:1497190).
運搬 often means carrying or transporting goods; 輸送 is the general term for transport, transportation, or conveyance (ent_seq:1538850).
気風 means the character, traits, or ethos of a group or place, matching the stated collective sense.
義理 directly covers social duty, obligation, honor, decency, and courtesy in this culturally specific sense.
守衛 is a guard or gatekeeper, while the English definition also includes caretaker and janitor; those are distinct jobs with different Japanese terms.
守備 usually means sports or military defense; 防御 is the general term for defense or protection (ent_seq:1520330).
収容 directly covers taking in, receiving, housing, seating, and admitting people, matching this accommodation sense.
上空 means the high-altitude sky or upper air, which matches the specified sky sense.
装備 suggests purpose-specific gear; 設備 directly covers general equipment, facilities, or installations (ent_seq:1386070).
体裁 can imply propriety or keeping up appearances; 外見 is the neutral term for outward appearance (ent_seq:1203520).
